text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A day of mourning is to be held today for the eight children killed in eastern Estonia when their bus crashed.
- Police discovered forged banknotes worth one million kroons.
- Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi softened his criticism of the cabinet ministers who came from the Reform Party, saying the work of the government as a whole was in line with expectations.

- Yevgeny Kogan, head of the electoral union Justice and a former leader of Interfront, which backed Estonia staying part of the former Soviet Union, is convinced his party can win five percent of the votes at the local council elections.
- 50 of the 101 parliament members have promised their support to the aims of trade union TALO to get a 20 percent pay rise for workers at cultural institutions.
- Litany, composed by Estonian Arvo Part, made it to the top of the classics chart of the U.S. music weekly Billboard.
- It would be easier for eastern European states to gain entry into NATO than into the EU, German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said in Berlin.
- Interior Minister Mart Raesk threatened to resign in parliament cut the ministry's 1997 budget.
- The government approved a draft law on pensions which will raise the retirement age for both men and women to 63 by 2016.
- Tallinna Kaubamaja department store is to open a branch in Helsinki in the first half of next year.
